newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids little changed, buoyed by weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids little changed, buoyed by weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices held relatively steady Tuesday in sluggish activity, with forecasts for colder East Coast weather and some low sulphur utility demand propping up prices, industry sources said.
"There's not a lot of demand but there seems to be a little buying interest," said one cash trader, noting prospects for two East Coast utility tenders this week.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged in the $18.00-18.25 a barrel range, with February paper talked steady to down slightly to the $17.50-75 area, traders said.
Traders said reports that a New England utility may soon tender for additional one percent helped support the grade.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour also held steady in the $19.00-25 area, helped by news of a NYPA spot tender for 200,000 barrels of HP for Feb 3-7 delivery. Fixed price bids are due by 1100 EST Wednesday, January 29.
High sulphurs in New York, helped by firmer bunkers, were flat to up slightly, traders said.
U.S. Gulf one percent was still at $16.50. Traders said USG three percent again eased slightly to $14.50-75 on reports HSFO (probably 4.0 pct) sold Monday at $14.15 (FOB Houston).
Cold weather headed East again boosted New York city gate gas prices by another 10 cents to the $3.60/mmBtu level. NYH one percent resid remained at a $2.88/mmBtu equivalent.
